COPILOT INSTRUCTIONS FOR CONTRIBUTORS AND THE AI ASSISTANT

Purpose
-------
This file captures repository-level rules and preferences for GitHub Copilot / AI assistant suggestions. Follow these when accepting or applying generated code. These are adapted from the sibling project (ultra-tracker) and tuned for ost-uploader (a .NET 8 desktop uploader).

Core decision order (apply in order)
1. Preserve public API and on-disk formats: do not change file formats, database schemas, CSV layout, or public method signatures without an explicit design discussion and an accompanying migration plan.
2. Match existing style and patterns: prefer the project's established patterns (MVVM, INotifyPropertyChanged, async/await, naming and formatting). Keep changes consistent with nearby code.
3. Prefer minimal, well-tested changes: prefer small, focused changes with unit tests or manual verification steps documented in the PR description.
4. Favour framework conventions: use .NET built-in APIs (System.Text.Json, IConfiguration, ILogger) over adding new dependencies unless a clear benefit is documented in the PR.
5. Security & secrets: never add credentials, API keys, or other secrets to the repository or generated code. Prefer configuration via environment variables or user secrets and document any runtime configuration required.

Follow-up rules (run after core decisions)
- Document behavior changes: update README, release notes, or in-code XML docs for any nontrivial behavior change.
- Keep UI behavior stable: for XAML/UI changes, preserve existing user workflows and accessibility considerations; include screenshots or reproduction steps when proposing UI changes.
- Compatibility: keep installers and packaging workflows compatible with supported OS targets (Windows for ost-uploader). If changing packaging, include testing steps.
- Licensing & attribution: follow repository license; do not add third-party code with incompatible licenses without approval.

Project-specific rules for ost-uploader
- Target framework: preserve net8.0 TFM in project files unless a separate task updates all projects.
- UI framework: ost-uploader is a WPF desktop app. Follow MVVM patterns already in the codebase. Avoid putting business logic in code-behind unless the change is small and justified.
- Async I/O: file and network operations should be asynchronous (async/await) and cancellable where reasonable.
- Serialization: prefer System.Text.Json for new serialization code; if Newtonsoft.Json is already used and pervasive, match existing usage.
- Tests: attach or update unit tests for business logic changes. For UI-only changes, document manual test steps in the PR.
- No new native dependencies: do not add native or platform-specific dependencies unless the change requires them and a CI/test plan exists.

What to do when Copilot proposes code
- Validate the proposal locally: build and run the solution, run affected tests, or perform the documented manual checks.
- Prefer explicit, short changes: prefer replacing a small function or adding a helper over bulk refactors generated by Copilot without tests.
- Write tests: where behavior changes, add unit tests or integration tests that demonstrate the expected behavior.
- PR description: when creating a PR with AI-suggested code, add a short sentence saying which parts were generated/assisted by Copilot and what was manually changed or reviewed.

Contact / escalation
If you are unsure whether a change is safe (schema change, TFM upgrade, new dependency), open an issue and discuss before merging.
